cells.tense: You are at the beginning of something you mean to build, and the blueprint is in your own hand.
cells.ask: Hand one unfinished piece of the plan to a person you trust to handle it wet.
cells.core:
You are at the beginning of something you mean to build, and the blueprint is in your own hand. The lines you draw hold. People around you move inside a shape you set, and they do not experience it as a cage — they experience it as a floor. You know which order things go in before anyone else does, and that knowing is quiet enough to look like common sense.

The balance holds. Before it hardens into the way things have always been done, hand one unfinished piece of it to someone you trust. Not the finished version — the model, still soft enough to take a thumbprint.
cells.sheetLine: You set the structure here, and you set it from clarity, not from needing to win.
cells.verb: planting the first real seed of what you mean to build
cells.place: in the part of a life where you draw the lines and set the shape things will keep

cells.tense: You are building for a future you cannot actually see, and the scaffolding has gone up further than the ground can carry.
cells.ask: Ask what the shape already in front of you is asking to be — and let the answer change the plan.
cells.core:
You are building for a future you cannot actually see, and the scaffolding has gone up further than the ground can carry. Every system you put in place is bracing for something that has not happened yet. You draw the lines tighter, name the roles sooner, close the openings before anyone can walk through them — and none of it makes the future arrive any calmer.

The structure stopped serving the thing it was built for. Set nothing new for a day. Ask what the shape already in front of you is asking to be, and let the answer move something.
cells.sheetLine: You are designing for a future you cannot see, and the structure is bracing instead of holding.
cells.verb: planting the first real seed of what you mean to build
cells.place: in the part of a life where you draw the lines and set the shape things will keep

cells.tense: You are standing in front of the shape you meant to build, and it has been a while since you picked up anything to draw with.
cells.ask: Draw one true line today — not the whole plan, just the one you can see clearly — and let that be enough to start.
cells.core:
You are standing in front of the shape you meant to build, and it has been a while since you picked up anything to draw with. The capacity to make order out of what is messy is still yours — you can see the container that would hold the thing, you just are not stepping into the role of the one who builds it. From the outside it looks like patience. From inside it is a held breath.

You do not need the whole plan. Draw one line today, the one you can see clearly, and let it be the first thing the structure rests on.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the shape and you are not setting it, and the waiting has become its own kind of structure.
cells.verb: planting the first real seed of what you mean to build
cells.place: in the part of a life where you draw the lines and set the shape things will keep

cells.tense: You are already organizing what is around you — drawing lines, setting order, deciding what goes where — and you are calling it just how things happened to turn out.
cells.ask: Settle one small thing this week in your own words, out loud, and let that be enough.
cells.core:
When this part of a life is going well, you are the one who makes the mess make sense. You walk into a tangle and walk out with a shape — who does what, in what order, starting when. People hand you chaos and get back something they can stand on, and they trust it because it is clear rather than loud. That trust is not an accident. It comes from the lines being drawn on purpose.

The shape is being set right now, and you are the one setting it. You draw the lines, decide what goes where, and then describe it as just how things turned out — as if the room organized itself. People come to you for the shape without either of you naming why. Settle one small thing this week in your own words, out loud, and let that be enough. The shape is yours, and it is being made now.
cells.sheetLine: You are setting the shape right now. The claim that it is yours has not been made.
cells.verb: planting the first real seed of what you mean to build
cells.place: in the part of a life where you draw the lines and set the shape things will keep
